subject: A pair of red shoes sits alone in an empty museum vitrine, lit from above, casting a shadow twice their size on the white wall behind.
Two red shoes move across a darkened stage as if waltzed by invisible hands, their motion caught mid-step, the rest of the theater swallowed in black.
Ruby slippers rest on a yellow brick road that dissolves into darkness at both ends, no figure nearby, no destination visible.
A long horizontal trail of small red footprints gradually fades from dark to invisible, as if the walker is slowly disappearing into the air.
A pair of red shoes stands in a doorway, three sources of light behind it (one warm, one cool, one flickering) casting three separate shadows forward onto the floor in different directions.
Red shoes rest on an open book among dozens of other open books, their pages blank and turning slightly as if from breath, no reader visible.
A single pair of red shoes sits on a dark floor surrounded by the soft blue-green glow of server lights blinking in sequence, as if the shoes are being read by machines.
Red shoes walk backward through heavy rain, their prints filling with water as fast as they're made, the figure holding them only a silhouette moving away.
A crowd of silhouettes bends toward a single pair of red shoes on the ground, all their hands extended but not touching, frozen in the moment before contact.
The stage is bare except for two red shoes standing upright where the dancer was, the spotlight still on them, the rest of the theater empty and dark.
Red shoes move across a floor as light breaks through a high window, their shadow shrinking as the sun rises, the motion still continuing though no one holds them.
Two red shoes sit motionless on a white surface in soft light, finally still, their shape so clear it casts almost no shadow at all.
